newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Uneximbank to sell 38 pct of Norilsk Nickel.
newsitem.headline: Russia Uneximbank to sell 38 pct of Norilsk Nickel.

text.p: Russia's Uneximbank commercial bank will sell its 38 percent stake in the giant Norilsk Nickel metals group in an investment tender, a bank spokesman said on Monday.

"We are offering 38 percent of the shares through a commercial tender," said Uneximbank spokesman Sergei Chernitsyn, adding, "the results will be known on August 5." The stake represents 51 percent of voting shares.
The winner must make a minimum investment of $300 million plus payments of social costs and debts owed by Norilsk to the state pension fund. The tender opens on July 22 and closes on August 1.

Up for tender are 47.88 million ordinary shares, each with a nominal value of 250 roubles, giving the stake a nominal value of 11.97 billion roubles. The shares will be sold in one lot, and will carry a starting price of 131.61 million Ecus.
Foreigners would probably not be allowed to bid, Chernitsyn said, adding that foreign ownership in the company was limited to 15 percent.
Uneximbank, one of Russia's most powerful commercial banks, has struggled to implement a rescue package for Norilsk, a struggling Soviet-era group. ($1=5,789)
